canonical.title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
canonical.sourceFilePath: 15. Tries/2. Problems/05. Maximum XOR of two numbers.cpp

narrative.title: The Cipher Mask Championship
narrative.scenario: A red-team exercise stores device keys as 32-bit words. The prize goes to the pair of devices whose keys disagree in the most significant bit positions — the pair whose XOR is largest. The analyzer inserts every key into a bit-wise trie, then walks each key against the trie, always chasing the branch that flips its current bit.
narrative.inputFormat: An array nums of n non-negative integers.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the maximum value of nums[i] XOR nums[j] over all pairs (i and j may be equal only in the trivial zero case; the meaningful answer uses distinct positions).

testCases.explanation: 5 XOR 25 = 28, the strongest disagreement pattern in the set.
91 XOR 36 = 127 — the seven low bits all disagree between the two keys.

hintLevels: Level 1: High bits dominate XOR — greedily decide the outcome bit by bit, most significant first.
Level 2: Insert every number as a 32-level binary path; for each query number, walk toward the opposite bit whenever the trie offers it.
Level 3: Chasing the opposite branch sets that result bit; the accumulated mask after 32 levels is the best XOR for that number.
